evidence_against: F2 — UNKNOWN dynamically; SUPPORTED static assurance gap: the Git wrapper inherits the process environment and invokes Git without disabling replacement objects. A replacement commit can preserve the expected root tree while changing the ancestry Git traverses. Consequently, root-tree equality alone does not establish that merge-base examined the parents of the raw named commit. No evidence establishes that replacement refs actually exist in the reviewed repository.

Proposed ancestry counterexample, NOT EXECUTED: using the supplied synthetic test fixture, create an unrelated root commit with baseTree, then replace that commit with another commit having the same tree and base as its parent. The predicted verifier result is exit 0 with three UNCHANGED paths, whereas ancestry with replacement objects disabled should return non-ancestor. This would be a false acceptance of provenance, not a missed source-content change.

F1 — CONFLICTED exact-commit assurance: HEX40 validates identifier syntax, not object type. The checks using SHA+'^{tree}' and merge-base permit peeling commit-like objects; there is no direct requirement that --head or inventory.main_commit name an object of type commit. An annotated-tag object SHA pointing to base is a proposed accepted input, despite being reported as compared_commit. Its immutable target limits the severity, but direct-commit typing is not established.

F3 — VERIFIED coverage limitation from the supplied test text: there are ten test calls sharing one synthetic repository, not ten independently initialized fixtures. They contain one mixed drift/missing-path case and nine rejection cases. No test exercises a successful exit-0 reconciliation, the current TYPE_MISMATCH branch, replacement-object ancestry, annotated-tag identifiers, or cross-environment ordering.

F3 — SUPPORTED portability defect: the harness passes new URL(...).pathname as the Node script filename. A URL pathname remains percent-encoded; a source directory containing a space can therefore produce a nonexistent filename containing %20. Windows file-URL paths also require platform conversion. This concerns test executability, not demonstrated production-verifier false acceptance.

F2 — VERIFIED diagnostic limitation from control flow: all target rev-parse/cat-file exceptions are absorbed. Resolution failure becomes MISSING; failure after SHA assignment becomes TYPE_MISMATCH. These outcomes fail closed, but missing entries, unavailable objects and Git operational failures are not distinguished. All merge-base failures likewise become 'not descended', including operational errors.

The supplied older v1 file lacks the per-source historical SHA/type checks present in embedded v1.1. The public drift receipt concerns compared commit 05f9daba3a8648c1d7c744fa5665b1014c968639, not PR head b2841b387106a2c5ae22b91eef8c59b786d73b16. Neither that receipt nor prose reporting earlier passes independently certifies this exact implementation.

hypotheses: F4 — proposed minimal replacement-object regression, NOT EXECUTED and not a repository-write request: reuse the supplied test fixture's git/run helpers and inventory. Define target=git('commit-tree',baseTree,'-m','unrelated-root'); replacement=git('commit-tree',baseTree,'-p',base,'-m','replacement-parent'); then establish git('replace',target,replacement). A separate spawnSync('git',['--no-replace-objects','merge-base','--is-ancestor',base,target],{cwd:dir}) should return status 1. The unmodified verifier run(inventory,target,baseTree) is predicted to return status 0, verified_all_paths=true and counts.UNCHANGED=3. Remove the synthetic replacement in fixture cleanup. A corrected verifier should reject this target. These are expected outcomes, not execution receipts.

Bounded remediation design for that proposed case, NOT APPLIED: the affected wrapper is execFileSync('git',args,...), and the affected ancestry operation is git(['merge-base','--is-ancestor',inventory.main_commit,head]). Prefix every verifier Git invocation with the global --no-replace-objects option, not just the ancestry invocation, so tree, source and ancestry checks use consistent replacement-disabled semantics. This addresses the proposed replacement-ref case only; repository redirection, legacy grafts and other environment assumptions still require explicit assurance.

Proposed direct-object-type regression, NOT EXECUTED: create an unsigned annotated tag pointing to base, obtain the tag object's full SHA, and independently confirm cat-file -t returns tag. Run the original inventory with that SHA as --head and baseTree as --expected-tree. Acceptance is predicted because the operations peel the tag. Bounded correction design: after establishing replacement-disabled Git semantics, require cat-file -t on each supplied commit anchor itself to equal commit before any peeling or ancestry check. Test annotated-tag inputs in both anchor positions.

Proposed harness portability regression, NOT EXECUTED: place the code and tests in a directory containing a space, with no literal percent-encoded counterpart, and separately exercise Windows paths. The affected expression is new URL('./2026-10-14__task2_r0_git_object_reconcile_v1_1.mjs',import.meta.url).pathname. The bounded correction is fileURLToPath from node:url before passing the filename to spawnSync.

Bounded additional semantic checks: an all-UNCHANGED exit-0 case; an all-present CHANGED exit-0 case; target blob-to-tree and tree-to-blob transitions requiring TYPE_MISMATCH and exit 2; baseline-tree mismatch; operational Git failures distinct from missing entries; malformed/repeated CLI flags; and ordering stability across locales. Compare expected classifications against independently generated Git objects, not only the verifier's summary flags.

Coverage-boundary check: families=[] is accepted and yields zero rows with verified_all_paths=true. Determine whether the external frozen-inventory binding permits that input. This is not established as a verifier defect because 'all listed paths' is vacuously true and empty private source families are present in the legitimate inventory. Completeness of the 36-path census requires a separate immutable inventory binding.
